body:
Your three requirements, and one result that came out differently than I wrote it.

## 1. Deadlock — and the negative control that contradicted my own rationale

I designed sorted acquisition (all claimants take locks in one global order, so no
cycle can form) and wrote into the module header that `--self-test` **proves** it, by
racing two processes that request the same two devices in **opposite** order. It went
green on the first run. Then I removed the sort and re-ran:

| variant | opposite-order pair | reading |
|---|---|---|
| as shipped | 0,0 in 2.1 s | pass |
| **sort removed**, rest intact | **0,0 in 2.1 s** | **the test never noticed** |
| sort removed **and** hold-and-wait restored | 3,3 in 15.1 s | real cycle — broken only by `--wait` expiring |

So the mechanism doing the work is **no hold-and-wait**: on contention the claimant
drops every lock it already holds before retrying, which breaks Coffman's hold-and-wait
condition outright. Sorting is real and kept as defence in depth — it is what would
still hold if `--wait` ever grew a blocking `flock(LOCK_EX)` path — but the self-test
does not discriminate on it, and the header now says exactly that.

That 3,3-in-15.1 s row is what makes the check non-vacuous at all. Without it, a test
that passes on *every* variant is a test that measures nothing.

## 2. In the GitHub release

jess had **no release workflow** — v0.6.0 was cut by hand and jess shipped no binary.
That is precisely why gale could read `with-device` but not run it, and why varve#130
had nothing to pin: a varve layer needs a signed release asset with a digest, not a
repo path.

`release.yml` builds on tag push for `x86_64/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` and
`aarch64/x86_64-apple-darwin`, emitting `with-device-<ver>-<triple>.tar.gz` +
`SHA256SUMS.txt` — the same shape every other PulseEngine repo publishes and that
`tools/deps/fetch.sh` already parses, so a consumer pins it like synth or meld.

**Honest scope:** `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` is cross-built and its self-test is
**skipped**. That asset ships unexecuted, and the workflow says so at the step rather
than implying coverage. It is the target the Pi will use, so it needs a real run there
before anyone trusts it.

## 3. Rust, mandatory

v0.1.0 Python → v0.2.0 crate at the same path. **Zero dependencies** — `flock(2)` is
declared with a bare `extern "C"`, so the binary headed for a signed layer has nothing
to vendor and nothing to audit but itself. `clippy -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`
clean.

## Also

New `bench-tool` CI job runs build + the CLI baseline + `--self-test` on every PR. A
lock that silently fails to exclude is worse than no lock — both agents then believe
they hold the probe — so that property is gated now, not remembered.

Finding recorded as **AFD-083**, linked `corrects` → AFD-081 and `traces-to` → DD-027.
`rivet validate`: **Result: PASS**.
title: feature: with-device in Rust, in the GH release, CI-gated — and the negative control that broke my own deadlock rationale (AFD-083)
